newsitem.title: USA: Norelco says pleased with court ruling on TV ads.
newsitem.headline: Norelco says pleased with court ruling on TV ads.

text.p: The parent company of Connecticut-based Norelco Consumer Products Co. said Tuesday it was pleased with a federal judge's ruling in the first round of the shaving company's court battle with rival Gillette Co.

"We don't have to pull any ads (off the air), we only have to modify future ads," Jon Kasle, vice president of corporate communications of Norelco parent company Philips Electronics North America Corp, a unit of Philips Electronics NV, told Reuters in an interview.

Gillette claims Norelco's ads -- which use animated images of a razor blade that spits fire and snaps with ferocious, razor-sharp teeth -- are deceptive. Gillette is seeking punitive and other damages.

Judge Reginald Lindsay of the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts issued a preliminary injunction Monday against Norelco's ads which claim that electric shavers cause less irritation than razor blades.

Lindsay ruled that the two-month-old ads, created by New York ad agency D'Arcy Masius Benton & Bowles, must include a "sufficiently conspicuous and contemporaneous statement" that a user of Norelco's Reflex Action electric razors should not expect less irritation until after three weeks.
Kasle said Norelco would abide by the court's ruling, but that Norelco was "thrilled" that it could retain the eye-catching images and basic visual thrust of its ads.
"We are pleased that the court found our studies to be supportive of the irritation claims made in our humorous ads," Norelco President Patrick Dinley said in a statement.
"The only place where irritation may be found is apparently in the hallways of our competitor, The Gillette Company," he said.
